claims.text: Module 4 is a concepts-tier lesson titled Data Contracts, requires module 3 Identities, must cover schemas, document types, indexes, contract-time decisions, and no triggers or joins, and completes through quiz challenge data-contracts.
A data contract is the registered schema for application data; document writes and changes succeed only when their data conforms to that schema.
The identity that registers a contract owns it, and only that owner can update it.
A contract contains named document types, each defining the fields, validation rules, indexes, and relevant behavior for one category of application record.
Document properties use JSON Schema-style types and constraints, distinguish required from optional fields, and require unique sequential positions starting at zero at each level.
Dash contracts must set additionalProperties to false wherever properties are defined.
Indexes are part of each document type and determine which fields can be filtered or sorted; non-indexed fields cannot be used for those operations apart from documented primary-key handling for $id.
Compound-index property order matters because usable queries must follow index prefix and ordering rules.

A unique index prevents two documents of one type from sharing the same indexed value combination when every indexed property is non-null, making it both a query structure and an enforced invariant for fully populated combinations. If any indexed property is null, uniqueness cannot be enforced for that document; the lesson's required string-typed slug cannot be null, so its example invariant applies.
An indexed string property has a documented maximum length of 63 characters.

Document boundaries, field constraints and requiredness, behavior, uniqueness, and query indexes are contract-time decisions; compatible additions are possible while renames, removals, type changes, and changes to existing unique indexes are restricted.
Ordinary application developers cannot deploy custom data triggers; Platform's hard-coded triggers are protocol logic used only by system contracts.
The document query surface targets one dataContractId and one documentTypeName and has no second source or join clause, so Platform provides no server-side relational joins.
The groupBy query option is ignored by regular document fetching and is used by the aggregate count, sum, and average query APIs.
Applications relate document types with stored identifier fields and separate fetches, or deliberate read-oriented duplication whose consistency the application manages.
As a concepts-tier quiz lesson before later writing and registration modules, module 4 should use a compact non-executable schema illustration rather than SDK registration or testnet code.

The pinned WASM SDK 4.1.1 exposes a DataContract constructor with ownerId, identityNonce, schemas, and an optional fullValidation flag; the independent fixture confirms construction of the corrected public schema, but does not treat that runtime check as proof that every documented index constraint is enforced.

conflicts.description: The authoritative data-contract reference limits indexed string properties to 63 characters, but the pinned WASM 4.1.1 DataContract constructor accepted test schemas whose indexed strings declared larger maxLength values.
conflicts.resolution: The lesson and fixture enforce the documented 63-character limit with a separate deterministic assertion. The WASM test is described only as a constructor check, not complete validation of documented deployment constraints.
